newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians clash with troops, strike in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians clash with troops, strike in Hebron.

text.p: Israel deployed troops across rooftops and alleyways in the divided West Bank city of Hebron as fresh clashes with Arab demonstrators erupted early on Wednesday, witnesses said.

Israeli soldiers and bulldozers sealed off an alley in the heart of the volatile town where Palestinians threw a home-made bomb at troops during clashes on Tuesday, wounding two. Soldiers wounded at least 35 Arabs in renewed violence on Tuesday.
Palestinian shops and stores were shut as the city and surrounding villages observed an all-day general strike called to protest anti-Moslem posters depicting the Prophet Mohammed as a pig.

Dozens of Palestinian youths took to the streets and threw stones at troops on the dividing line between Israeli- and PLO-ruled sectors of Hebron, witnesses said. Israeli troops fired rubber bullets and teargas to disperse the protesters.

Soldiers broke through the strike-sealed door of a Palestinian school with a sledgehammer and troops burst through the building to deploy on rooftops overlooking the narrow alleyways of Hebron's casbah.
Witnesses said Israeli bulldozers worked during the night, shovelling bricks to block entrances to the 20-metre (yard) long alley in the Israeli-controlled section of the divided town.

"The army sealed off an alley in Hebron overnight where home-made bombs were thrown recently at soldiers and border policemen, among them the bomb that wounded two soldiers yesterday," an army spokesman said.
Israeli soldiers declared the area a closed military zone after Palestinian security officials tried to prevent them from blocking entrances to the alley, witnesses said.
Israel Radio said the army had sent in reinforcements.

Israeli police are holding a 25-year-old Jewish woman suspected of pasting posters on Hebron storefronts picturing a pig donning an Arab headdress with the word Mohammad written on it in Arabic and English.
The pig was portrayed stomping with one foot on the Moslem holy book, the Koran, while holding a pen in the other. Islam and Judaism regard pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other Israeli leaders have repeatedly condemned the posters -- the latest spark to ignite violence in volatile Hebron.

Israeli troops have clashed with Palestinian protesters almost daily since Israel's groundbreaking of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last March plunged peacemaking with the PLO into crisis.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO-rule in January but troops stayed on to guard 400 Jewish settlers who live in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city revered by Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
